about.title: How Field Shift decides
about.lead: Built for NASA Space Apps 2026 for the dry, red Barind tract, where boro rice is pulling the water table down.
about.s1: Eight rotations common in Barind are scored on water, soil health, profit and climate risk, using NASA POWER rainfall and heat, cached SMAP root-zone moisture and MODIS greenness, and SRDI soil samples for the union. Your priority sliders weight the scores.
about.s2t: Pick one, and say how sure
about.s2: A System One decision model picks one rotation from the allowed list and gives a confidence. Below the confidence bar, the pick is flagged for review. Without the model, the top score wins.
about.s3: The same model reads English and Bangla market headlines for an early glut. Offline, a keyword scan of the same headlines stands in.
about.s4: The zone plan for the upazila stops one crop taking every field. The crop goes to the fields where it fits best; other fields move to the next suitable crop, and a farm that gives up the top crop is first for it next season.
about.s5: A language model only explains the assignment, in English and Bangla. It does not choose the crop or change any score.
sources: NASA POWER: rainfall, temperature, soil wetness
NASA AppEEARS: SMAP L4 soil moisture and MODIS NDVI (prefetched)
SRDI via BARC Crop Zoning: soil samples and fertilizer doses
Market headlines in English and Bangla
about.caveat: Crop margins and some traits are still placeholders. Treat the advice as a starting point for a conversation with your extension officer.
